_names: Terminologia Anatomica individual terms (explicitly public domain)
_definitions: Gray's Anatomy 1918, original scan (PD-US) for `femur`, which already existed in this repo. The `tibia` and `fibula` entries were written for this module in the same register and are NOT presented as verbatim quotations from Gray's.
_geometry: Classical segmentation, NO machine learning and NO licensed model: atlas-pipeline/segment_knee_ct.py on Visible Human frozenCT slices 2300-2470. Bone contrast is the one thing this frozen cadaver reproduces faithfully, so HU thresholding at 300 plus 3D connected components plus position is sufficient, and it is free.
_why_not_a_model: The only model offering tibia, fibula and patella is TotalSegmentator's `appendicular_bones`, which sits in the package's own `commercial_models` register and calls sys.exit(1) without a licence key. VISTA3D / NV-Segment-CT was checked against its own vista3d/data/jsons/label_dict.json and has NO tibia, fibula or patella either — its skeleton stops at femur, hip, humerus, scapula, clavicula, skull, sternum, sacrum and vertebrae. So a classical pipeline was built rather than blocking the product or buying a licence.
_how_the_bones_are_told_apart: Measured, not assumed. 3D connected components inside a leg mask over VHP 2300-2470 gave exactly six bones with no ambiguity: tibia 102074 and 99664 voxels spanning z 31-170 at |relx| 0.65, median 643-650 HU; distal femur 64958 and 61384 voxels spanning z 0-42 at |relx| 0.58, median 427-434 HU; fibula 14427 and 13708 voxels spanning z 49-170 at |relx| 0.80, median 791-834 HU. Z-EXTENT separates femur (superior, stops at the joint) from the leg bones (start at the joint, run to the bottom of the crop). SIZE separates tibia from fibula, a 7x ratio in both legs. LATERALITY is used only as a CHECK - the fibula must be the more lateral of the pair, and it passed on both sides - never to assert a side.
_the_arm_trap: The cadaver's forearms and hands lie beside the thighs at this level. A naive 'body component over 4000 px' rule admits them, which is exactly how the whole-body run came to label an arm bone `femur` (its voxels sat at relx +0.82 to +0.97, hard against the body edge). Here the legs are taken as the TWO LARGEST components on every slice, which excludes forearms, hands and the freezing container.
_why_no_patella: NOT RELIABLY AVAILABLE, and deliberately absent rather than approximated. At the knee the epiphyseal bone is trabecular under a thin cortex, so a 300 HU threshold fragments it: the femoral component breaks into 20-22 separate in-plane parts at its mid-slice, against 1 for the solid tibial shaft, and no patella survives as a component of its own above the 3000-voxel floor. Pointing a pin at a trabecular fragment and calling it a patella would be a fabricated label. Requires either `appendicular_bones` under licence, or a dedicated patella routine using a lower threshold with an anterior-position constraint - future work, not a claim.
_why_no_tarsals_metatarsals_phalanges: Not attempted in this module. The foot needs its own crop and the same measurement-first treatment; the slices exist (VHP 2700-2882) and this is tracked as future work rather than silently omitted.
_why_no_sides: No side is asserted, consistent with every other module. One pin per connected component still gives the reviewer both legs.

femur.name: Femur
femur.definition: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the skeleton.

tibia.name: Tibia
tibia.definition: The tibia is the medial and larger of the two bones of the leg, transmitting the weight of the body from the femur to the foot.

fibula.name: Fibula
fibula.definition: The fibula is the slender lateral bone of the leg, bearing little weight but giving attachment to muscles and forming the lateral malleolus at the ankle.

_why_caps: Both legs are in every axial cut, so each bone appears twice. Two pins is the whole story; more only saturates the gutters.
